challenges: Preserving Strict Micro-Budget Discipline Post-Atomic Monster Merger: Preventing BTL crew inflation, VFX creep, and shooting-day overruns from eroding Blumhouse's signature $3M-$12M break-even moat across a larger combined slate.

Pre-Greenlight Concept, Title & Trailer Hook Validation: Quantitatively separating theatrical event horror premises (M3GAN, Five Nights at Freddy's, The Black Phone) from streaming-grade concepts BEFORE committing Universal P&A.

Horror Box-Office Saturation & Audience Jump-Scare Fatigue: Engineering fresh sub-genre tonal twists and social-first viral characters (TikTok/Shorts memeability) when generic supernatural formulas underperform.

Complex Multi-Tier Back-End Profit Participation & Guild Residual Accounting: Automating transparent waterfall reporting across theatrical, PVOD, Pay-1 streaming, and merchandise pools for dozens of profit-participating directors, actors, and crews.

Expanding Blumhouse Games Interactive Pipeline: Applying the proven micro-budget film playbook (<$10M development cap, high creative freedom) to indie horror video games without multi-year scope slip.
